title: Reddit will make users log in as Google’s AI search cuts its traffic
content:
Reddit is moving to a “logged-in-only experience”, chief executive Steve Huffman told shareholders on Thursday. For most of its 21-year history, anyone could read the site without an account.
The plan came with Reddit’s third-quarter results, which beat analysts’ revenue estimates. In his shareholder letter, Huffman said search traffic was “down meaningfully” and that the drop sped up late in the quarter. Reddit will start testing a Reddit login requirement in select markets outside the US in the fourth quarter.
“It’s a big one for us, and it’s a big one for me,” Huffman wrote.
He gave three reasons. Logged-in users get a better experience, and they give Reddit more signals for ad targeting. The change also protects “Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data” and helps Reddit adapt to new regulations around the world, he wrote.
What logged-out visitors will still see
Reddit has not decided how much of the site will stay open. In a post on Reddit, Huffman said the front page should stay available without an account. People arriving from search or a shared link should still see the post they were sent to, he wrote.
“Reddit is so big now that without some personalization, it’s just not relevant. Or even worse, it just doesn’t work,” Huffman wrote.
He said the “vast majority” of the scraping of Reddit’s data happens through logged-out browsing. Users will not have to give their real name to log in. A day earlier, Reddit announced two new feeds, a personalised For You feed and a Following feed of joined communities.
Reddit is also relaunching incognito mode in its app, Huffman and chief operating officer Jen Wong told Sara Fischer of Axios. It will be read-only, so users cannot comment or vote in it.
Users did not welcome the post. It stood at 0 upvotes with about 200 comments late on Thursday, Tom McKay reported for Gizmodo.
Google’s AI search and the traffic
Search traffic fell by more than 1 million referrals a week on average in October, according to the letter. If that rate continues, Reddit’s daily active users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter, from about 130 million.
Huffman put the drop down to Google’s AI Mode and AI Overviews, which answer questions on the search page itself.
“The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic. Not for us, and not to anybody, as far as I know,” Huffman said on the earnings call, as Jay Peters reported for The Verge.
This week, Google said its AI Mode searches earn less than regular search. After its second-quarter results, Reddit’s stock fell 20% over the same Google worries.
“Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that’s largely because of me, I’ve been holding that line,” Huffman told Jonathan Vanian of CNBC.
Data deals, ads and the shares
Reddit still licenses its data to AI companies, and its two biggest data partners are OpenAI and Google, CNBC reported. Huffman told CNBC that Reddit remains “in negotiations” with Google over its deal. Reddit sued Anthropic and Perplexity over scraping in 2025. It is also killing its RSS feeds. In July, TNW reported that Reddit may cut Google off from its content.
Wong told Riley Griffin of Bloomberg that the Google talks are “complicated”. The outcomes include, “if it’s strategic, to not renew a partnership”, she said.
Revenue rose 53% to $895m in the third quarter, and ad revenue rose 54% to $847m. Other revenue, which includes data licensing, rose 35% to $48m. Daily active users grew 12% to 130.3 million worldwide but fell 2% in the US, to 50.7 million.
Logged-out daily users grew 17%, faster than logged-in users at 7%, the results show. Wong told Axios that logged-in users are about five times as engaged as logged-out ones. She put the figure at roughly 10 times in her interview with Bloomberg.
Reddit expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1bn to $1.03bn, below analysts’ estimates of $1.05bn, according to CNBC. Its shares fell about 18% in after-hours trading on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. Wong told Bloomberg the move could limit Reddit’s reach in the short term.
“I think that’s a trade that makes sense for the long term,” Wong said.

report.summary: Reddit将推行强制登录，应对谷歌AI搜索的流量分流
report.background: Reddit成立21年来一直允许未登录访问，是少数仍开放公开抓取的平台。谷歌AI Overviews和AI Mode在搜索结果页直接给出答案，用户不再点击进入网站，导致Reddit搜索引荐流量10月每周减少超100万次。三季度Reddit营收8.95亿美元、同比增53%，但四季度指引低于预期，股价盘后跌约18%；今年早些时候它已因同类担忧跌过20%。Reddit一边把内容授权给OpenAI和谷歌，一边起诉Anthropic和Perplexity抓取，还宣布停掉RSS订阅源，如今把强制登录当作保住数据和广告定向的应对措施。
key_points: 谷歌AI搜索直接给出答案，用户不再点进Reddit，10月每周少掉超100万次引荐，CEO称“AI Mode不给任何网站带流量”
Reddit将在四季度于美国以外市场试点强制登录，首页和搜索、分享直达的帖子仍可匿名查看
官方理由是登录用户更活跃、广告定向更准，并减少未登录浏览带来的数据抓取；CEO承认绝大多数抓取来自未登录访问
财务上很赚钱但增长承压：三季度营收8.95亿、广告8.47亿美元，但四季度指引10亿至10.3亿美元，低于预期
未登录日活同比增长17%，快于登录用户的7%，说明被限制的正是增长最快的人群，Reddit用户对此强烈不满
report.impact: 对AI行业，公开可抓取的高质量语料正在减少，模型训练数据的获取成本会上升，内容方与AI公司之间的授权谈判将更强势。对开发者，免费数据源收紧，依赖Reddit内容的搜索、RAG和舆情工具需要转向官方API或授权，抓取合规风险加大。对普通用户，找答案的门槛变高，需要注册账号才能深度浏览，但个性化信息流体验可能更好，也可能进一步把流量锁在平台内。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：TollBit、ScalePost.ai 等按次计费的内容授权与爬虫结算方案；Cloudflare pay-per-crawl 的抓取付费机制；Profound、Otterly 等监测品牌在AI搜索中被引用的GEO工具；以及 Reddit 官方 Data API 和开源 PRAW 库，用于合规获取社区数据。
